blocks.text: Mission Farms: what the ground is and what governs it

items.t: Fee-simple parcels are the only acreage form: A Mission farm purchase is a fee-simple title purchase: no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fee — City or FVRD rules by jurisdiction, ALR rules where the parcel is in the reserve, and any registered covenants on title govern.

Serviced vs unserviced: What it does document: under the Water Sustainability Act, groundwater used for non-domestic purposes such as irrigation requires a water licence and payment of water fees and rentals before the water can lawfully be used; domestic groundwater use does not require authorization. And under Fraser Health's rules, a home or building with indoor plumbing not connected to a community sewer must use an onsite sewage system complying with the Sewerage System Regulation, and only an Authorized Person (a Professional Engineer or a Registered Onsite Wastewater Practitioner) can design, install, repair, maintain or inspect a sewerage system. Parcel-level servicing: Not confirmed until the water licence position and the Authorized Person's filings for that parcel are read.

A "Mission" mailing address can carry rural taxes: Hatzic Prairie (FVRD Area F) and Hatzic Island (Area G) sit in the rural tax regime — 5% after July 2 plus 5% after October 31 under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11 — while Hatzic Bench, blocks away in name, is City of Mission ground under the flat 10% penalty after July 2. The folio and the jurisdiction map answer it; the district name does not.

The zoning minimums in search results are from a repealed bylaw: Mission's zoning now runs under Bylaw 5949-2020 as amended, but mirrors of predecessor Bylaw 5050-2009 — with its RU80 / RU36 / RU16 minimums (8.0 ha / 3.6 ha / 1.6 ha) — still circulate.

Farm classification has a hard calendar date: A continuing farmer must apply by October 31 for the following taxation year, and the income thresholds scale with the operation's size — a buyer who closes after that date without a plan can lose the classification, and its tax treatment, for a year.

The suite rule on ALR land is narrower than in town: A secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence — a separate garden suite or coach house on ALR land must instead fit the one-additional-residence size caps (90 m² / 186 m²) and the local bylaw.

Mission farm land is the rural east and north of the city, not the urban core: the farm districts are Dewdney–Deroche, Durieu, Hatzic, Lake Errock and Stave Falls, reached along Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) and the Dewdney Trunk Road corridor.

This page's ground straddles two governments, and the split is exact: Stave Falls and Steelhead are inside the City of Mission, Hatzic Bench is inside the City, Hatzic Prairie is Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area F, and Hatzic Island is FVRD Electoral Area G.

The Fraser River is the farm belt's south edge: the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area, at the city's west end, is bordered to the south by the Fraser River and Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) lands.

Mission is in the Fraser Valley Regional District, not Metro Vancouver, which is why its transit, regional taxes and planning referrals run through the FVRD and BC Transit rather than Metro Vancouver and TransLink.

Farm families are served by School District No. 75 (Mission) rural schools including Deroche Elementary at 10340 N Deroche Rd, Dewdney Elementary at 37151 Hawkins-Pickle Rd and Hatzic Elementary at 8465 Draper St, with catchments set by home address.

Mission farms trade as whole fee-simple farm parcels — working farms, bare agricultural land and rural acreages with farm potential — bought whole with their buildings, water and septic position, not as serviced lots.

There is no bare-land strata farm product here, and on ALR parcels the strata form is barred outright: residences in the ALR cannot be stratified without the Agricultural Land Commission's permission, because depositing a strata plan is a subdivision.

The province's own farm inventory describes Mission's pattern: the BC Ministry of Agriculture's Agricultural Land Use Inventory (2011 inventory, published 2013) found a greater number of smaller farms than larger operations in Mission, across a variety of livestock and crop operations.

The ALR share is small and dated, so check current: that same provincial inventory puts Mission's ALR at 1,539 hectares, nearly 7% of the District of Mission's 22,422 hectare land area at the time of the 2011 inventory, as the figure is more than 12 months old.

blocks.text: Mission Farms: rules that affect buyers

items.t: City-side zoning is Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020, as amended — the City's 2025 housekeeping package amends it as Bylaw 6354-2025-5949(187) — while FVRD-side parcels are zoned under FVRD bylaws, so the governing bylaw is a jurisdiction check first.

The current Official Community Plan is OCP Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026, which replaced and repealed OCP Bylaw 6350-2025 with the vision, land use framework, mapping and policy direction unchanged and a Regional Context Statement added.
The City's Rural Mission Strategy — its plan to recognize, protect and enhance Mission's rural areas, building on the OCP — is finalized and posted by the City.

ALR subdivision requires Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) approval, and the residence caps are fixed: one principal residence per parcel at a maximum 500 square metres, a secondary suite only inside the principal residence, and one additional residence without an ALC application where conditions are met — capped at 90 square metres on parcels of 40 hectares or less and 186 square metres on larger parcels, if local bylaws also permit it.
Subdivision and servicing on the City side runs under the Development and Subdivision Control Bylaw 5650-2017, listed in the City's own bylaws library.

Flood rules are bylaw-set on the low ground: Mission's Floodplain Management Bylaw 4027-2007 specifies floodplain setbacks and flood construction levels, including a 60 metre setback from the natural boundary of the Fraser River, 15 metres from any other stream, and 7.5 metres from the inboard toe of a dyke.

Farm classification has three income tiers, never one flat figure: $2,500 of gross farm income at farm gate prices on a farm operation of 0.8 to 4 hectares, $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 hectares above that, and $10,000 on operations under 0.8 hectares, with applications by October 31 for the next taxation year.

blocks.text: Mission Farms: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The same farm search crosses two tax clocks: a Stave Falls parcel answers to the City (flat 10% penalty after July 2), while a Hatzic Prairie parcel a short drive away answers to the rural regime (5% after July 2, plus 5% after October 31) — the tax folio, not the address, says which.

The old zoning bylaw still circulates: Mission's zoning now runs under Bylaw 5949-2020 as amended, but Bylaw 5050-2009 texts still appear in non-municipal mirrors, and rural minimum parcel sizes quoted from them may be predecessor figures.
City taxes on farm-belt parcels can carry diking levies on top of the municipal, school, regional district and BC Assessment levies, per the City's tax rates page.

A farm home not on community sewer must use an onsite sewage system complying with the Sewerage System Regulation, and only an Authorized Person can design, install, repair, maintain or inspect a sewerage system, per Fraser Health.

blocks.text: Mission Farms: development and new projects

items.t: Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area (SCPA) neighbourhood planning, west Mission, City of Mission planning process under Policy LAN.64(C), adopted February 18, 2020: the SCPA is 1,392 hectares (3,440 acres) inside the urban growth boundary, and neighbourhood plans are required for areas anticipating growth in density or experiencing development pressure — status: planning process in place (as of November 3, 2026).

Official Community Plan Development Permit Area (DPA) Guidelines Review, City of Mission: the City is updating the DPA guidelines in the OCP, with a further public hearing notice issued for August 17, 2026 — hillside and environmentally sensitive farm-edge lots are the parcels whose buildable area a DPA can set — status: in review (as of November 3, 2026).

City of Mission property taxes for 2026 were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, and a flat 10% penalty is added to any current balances outstanding, including unclaimed home owner grants, on July 3, 2026; the City states it has no authority to waive or modify the penalty.

Tax rates are set by class each year under the City's tax rates framework, with municipal rates set by the City, school rates set by the Province, regional district rates set by the Fraser Valley Regional District, and additional taxes levied for diking.

Development cost charges (DCCs) are imposed under Development Cost Charge Bylaw 6348-2025, adopted May 5, 2025, and apply to every person who obtains approval of a subdivision, a building permit for a commercial, industrial or institutional use, or a building permit for a residential building with more than one dwelling unit other than a secondary suite.

The DCC bylaw's stated purposes are the capital costs of sewage, water, drainage, fire protection, police, highway and solid waste and recycling facilities, and providing and improving park land, to service the development charged.

Amenity Cost Charges (ACCs) are imposed under Amenity Cost Charge Bylaw 6349-2025, also adopted May 5, 2025, replacing the Community Amenity Contribution for developers, payable at subdivision approval or building permit issuance.
Mission is a designated taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax — the Province's list names the District of Mission — so residential owners must complete the annual declaration.

Mission City Station is the eastern terminus of the West Coast Express, on the line running through Port Coquitlam, Coquitlam Central, Moody Centre and Port Moody-side stations to Waterfront — the commuter rail link for the farm districts west of the city.
Local buses are BC Transit, not TransLink: the Central Fraser Valley Transit System serves Mission, and its Mission routes include the 35 Hatzic route into the farm district east of downtown.
The Valley Connector bus routes link Mission and Abbotsford across the Fraser River on the Abbotsford–Mission Highway (Highway 11), the same crossing a farm operator uses for the Abbotsford side.

blocks.text: Mission Farms: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the flood construction level and setback for the parcel first on low ground: Mission's Floodplain Management Bylaw 4027-2007 governs City-side parcels, and in the Silverdale area the bylaw's Fraser River flood construction level is approximately 9.1 metres geodetic at the east side and 8.6 metres at the west side.

Check the FVRD regime on the other side of the boundary: Hatzic Island, in Electoral Area G, sits inside the Fraser River floodplain under the FVRD Floodplain Management Bylaw 0681, 2005, with a flood construction level of 9.3 metres geodetic and a minimum ponding elevation of 5.2 metres.

Check ALR status per parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission mapping by parcel identifier (PID) or civic address before pricing any residence, subdivision or non-farm use; the ALC states its online tools are for general reference, with official confirmation from its Mapping and GIS team.

faq.q: Can I irrigate from the well?
faq.a: Only with the water position confirmed: under the Water Sustainability Act, groundwater used for non-domestic purposes such as irrigation requires a water licence (and water fees/rentals) before it can lawfully be used; domestic groundwater use does not require authorization. Confirm the licence position for the operation before offering.

faq.q: Is the septic system a diligence item?
faq.a: Yes. A building with indoor plumbing not connected to community sewer must use an onsite system complying with the Sewerage System Regulation, and only an Authorized Person can design, install, repair, maintain or inspect it — ask for the Authorized Person's filings.

faq.q: City taxes or rural taxes — which apply to a "Mission" farm address?
faq.a: The jurisdiction's, not the mailing address's. City of Mission ground: due July 2, 2026, flat 10% penalty on balances outstanding July 3, 2026. FVRD electoral-area ground: the rural regime — 5% after July 2 plus 5% after October 31 (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11). Hatzic is the trap: Bench is City, Prairie is Area F, Island is Area G.

faq.q: Is this farm inside the City of Mission or the FVRD — and why does it matter?
faq.a: It decides the tax penalty, the zoning bylaw and the planning authority. Stave Falls, Steelhead and Hatzic Bench are City ground, where a flat 10% penalty applies to unpaid taxes after July 2; Hatzic Prairie (Area F) and Hatzic Island (Area G) are FVRD rural ground under the separate rural regime of 5% after July 2 plus 5% after October 31. A Mission mailing address settles nothing — check the parcel's tax folio.

faq.q: Can I build a second house on a Mission farm?
faq.a: The principal residence itself is capped at 500 square metres, a secondary suite is permitted only inside it, and City of Mission or FVRD bylaws must also allow the additional residence.

faq.q: How much income must the farm produce to keep farm classification?
faq.a: It depends on the operation's size, in three tiers: $2,500 of gross farm income at farm gate prices for an operation of 0.8 to 4 hectares; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 hectares for a larger operation; and $10,000 for an operation under 0.8 hectares. A continuing farmer applies by October 31 for the next taxation year, and a parcel that stops meeting its tier loses the classification.

faq.q: Can I irrigate from the well or creek?
faq.a: Only with the licence position confirmed. Under the Water Sustainability Act, groundwater used for a non-domestic purpose such as irrigation requires a water licence, with water fees and rentals payable, before the water can lawfully be used; domestic groundwater use does not require authorization. Ask for the licence, or evidence a licence is not needed, in the diligence package for any farm that depends on irrigation.

In the city's rural districts — the board's rural Mission sub-areas are Dewdney Deroche, Durieu, Hatzic, Hemlock, Lake Errock, Mission West, Stave Falls and Steelhead, and the live mission-farms feed's listing at the time of reading sat in Dewdney Deroche.
